site.name: Awesome Agentic DevSecOps
site.tagline: A curated atlas of AI agents that secure the software lifecycle — from threat modeling to SOC response.

categories.title: Threat Modeling & Design
categories.blurb: Agents that reason about architecture and attack surface before a line of code ships.

categories.title: Code Security & Review
categories.blurb: AI reviewers and fixers that find, triage, and patch vulnerabilities in source code and pull requests.

categories.title: Dependencies & Supply Chain
categories.blurb: Agents watching what you import — malicious packages, risky upgrades, and reachability.

categories.title: Infrastructure, Cloud & Kubernetes
categories.blurb: AI for IaC remediation, cluster diagnosis, and cloud-native runtime security.

categories.title: Offensive Security & Pentesting
categories.blurb: Autonomous red teams: agents that probe, exploit, fuzz, and validate — so defenders find it first.

categories.title: SOC, Detection & Response
categories.blurb: AI analysts that triage alerts, investigate incidents, and write detections around the clock.

categories.title: LLM & Agent Security
categories.blurb: Securing the AI itself — red teaming, guardrails, and scanners for models and agentic workflows.

categories.title: Compliance & Governance
categories.blurb: Agents that collect evidence, map controls, and keep audits continuous instead of annual.

categories.title: Frameworks & Building Blocks
categories.blurb: The foundations for building your own security agents — orchestration, tools, and MCP servers.

agents.name: STRIDE GPT
agents.description: AI-powered threat modeling that generates STRIDE threat models, attack trees, and mitigations from an application description.

agents.name: IriusRisk Jeff
agents.description: AI threat-modeling assistant inside IriusRisk that turns architecture diagrams and design docs into draft threat models.

agents.name: Claude Code Security Review
agents.description: GitHub Action from Anthropic that runs Claude against every pull request for semantic, context-aware security review.

agents.name: Aardvark (Codex Security)
agents.description: OpenAI's agentic security researcher: continuously scans repos, validates exploitability in a sandbox, and proposes patches. Now part of Codex Security.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot Autofix
agents.description: AI-generated fixes for CodeQL code-scanning alerts, proposed directly on pull requests via GitHub Advanced Security.

agents.name: Semgrep Assistant
agents.description: AI layer of the Semgrep AppSec platform that triages findings, filters false positives, and drafts remediation guidance.

agents.name: Snyk Agent Fix
agents.description: Snyk's DeepCode AI engine powering automated vulnerability fixes and self-healing pull requests, trained on curated security data.

agents.name: GitLab Duo Vulnerability Resolution
agents.description: GitLab's AI suite that explains SAST vulnerabilities and opens merge requests to resolve them inside the DevSecOps platform.

agents.name: Corgea
agents.description: AI AppSec engineer that scans with business-logic context, filters false positives, and auto-generates fixes as pull requests.

agents.name: Mobb
agents.description: Automatic vulnerability fixer that consumes SAST reports (Snyk, Checkmarx, CodeQL, Semgrep) and commits verified remediations.

agents.name: Pixee
agents.description: Automated product-security engineer (pixeebot) that continuously hardens code and fixes findings through pull requests.

agents.name: ZeroPath
agents.description: AI-native SAST that finds business-logic and code vulnerabilities and ships PR-ready patches.

agents.name: DryRun Security
agents.description: Contextual security analysis for pull requests using AI agents that reason about authz, injection, and business-logic risk.

agents.name: Vulnhuntr
agents.description: LLM-based static analyzer that autonomously chains multi-step, remotely exploitable vulnerabilities in Python code — credited with real 0-days.

agents.name: Ghost Security
agents.description: Agentic application-security platform whose autonomous agents map applications, APIs, and vulnerabilities at enterprise scale.

agents.name: Socket
agents.description: Supply-chain security that uses AI to analyze package behavior and block malicious or risky open-source dependencies before they land.

agents.name: Endor Labs
agents.description: Reachability-based SCA with AI agents that review code changes, prioritize exploitable dependency risk, and guide safe upgrades.

agents.name: Aikido Security
agents.description: Code-to-cloud security platform with AI AutoFix spanning dependencies, SAST, secrets, and IaC findings.

agents.name: K8sGPT
agents.description: CNCF tool that scans Kubernetes clusters and explains problems in plain English — SRE expertise encoded as analyzers with pluggable LLM backends.

agents.name: kubectl-ai
agents.description: AI-powered Kubernetes agent from Google that translates natural-language intent into safe kubectl operations.

agents.name: HolmesGPT
agents.description: 24/7 AI on-call agent that investigates alerts from Prometheus, PagerDuty, and more by pulling live cluster data and correlating root cause.

agents.name: Gomboc.ai
agents.description: Deterministic AI remediation for cloud infrastructure: generates policy-compliant fixes for Terraform and CloudFormation.

agents.name: Sysdig Sage
agents.description: AI cloud-security analyst built on runtime insights — multi-step reasoning over CNAPP findings from detection to remediation.

agents.name: kagent
agents.description: CNCF framework for running agentic AI natively in Kubernetes — declarative agents and MCP tools for DevOps, troubleshooting, and security operations.

agents.name: XBOW
agents.description: Autonomous penetration tester that reached #1 on HackerOne's US leaderboard, finding and validating exploits without human operators.

agents.name: PentestGPT
agents.description: GPT-powered penetration-testing assistant that guides recon, exploitation, and privilege escalation — backed by USENIX Security research.

agents.name: PentAGI
agents.description: Fully autonomous multi-agent pentesting system — specialized agents with isolated Docker tooling, long-term memory, and reporting.

agents.name: hackingBuddyGPT
agents.description: Research framework from TU Wien for building LLM agents that attempt privilege escalation and web pentests autonomously.

agents.name: HexStrike AI
agents.description: MCP server that lets AI agents orchestrate 150+ security tools — nmap, Burp, Metasploit — for automated recon and exploitation workflows.

agents.name: BurpGPT
agents.description: Burp Suite extension that adds LLM-powered passive scanning and traffic analysis to web security testing.

agents.name: Nebula
agents.description: AI-powered ethical-hacking assistant that wraps nmap, ZAP, and other tools with natural-language control.

agents.name: OSS-Fuzz-Gen
agents.description: Google's LLM framework that generates and improves fuzz targets for OSS-Fuzz — already surfacing real-world vulnerabilities.

agents.name: Google Big Sleep
agents.description: Project Zero × DeepMind agent that hunts memory-safety bugs in real software — found an exploitable SQLite flaw before release.

agents.name: Atlantis
agents.description: Team Atlanta's cyber-reasoning system that won DARPA's AI Cyber Challenge — autonomous vulnerability discovery and patching at scale.

agents.name: Buttercup
agents.description: Trail of Bits' open-sourced AIxCC cyber-reasoning system: agents that autonomously find and patch vulnerabilities in C and Java.

agents.name: Cybench
agents.description: Stanford benchmark evaluating LLM agents on professional CTF tasks — the reference eval for offensive agent capability.

agents.name: Escape
agents.description: Agentic DAST for APIs and business logic — AI agents explore, attack, and validate findings against running applications.

agents.name: Microsoft Security Copilot
agents.description: Microsoft's generative-AI security suite with agents for phishing triage, alert investigation, and posture across Defender and Sentinel.

agents.name: CrowdStrike Charlotte AI
agents.description: Agentic security analyst for the Falcon platform — bounded autonomous reasoning for detection triage and response.

agents.name: SentinelOne Purple AI
agents.description: AI security analyst that turns natural language into threat hunts, summarizes incidents, and automates investigation on Singularity.

agents.name: Dropzone AI
agents.description: AI SOC analyst that autonomously investigates every alert end-to-end, producing decision-ready reports without playbooks.

agents.name: Prophet Security
agents.description: Agentic AI SOC platform that triages and investigates alerts automatically, cutting response times from hours to minutes.

agents.name: Radiant Security
agents.description: AI-powered SOC that performs deep triage on 100% of alerts and proposes tailored response actions.

agents.name: Intezer
agents.description: Autonomous SOC that emulates a tier-1 analyst — investigates alerts, reverse-engineers files, and escalates only what matters.

agents.name: Torq HyperSOC
agents.description: Hyperautomation platform whose agentic AI runs SOC case investigation and remediation workflows at machine speed.

agents.name: Simbian
agents.description: AI agents for security operations that autonomously handle alert triage, threat hunting, and security questionnaires.

agents.name: Uncoder AI
agents.description: SOC Prime's AI for detection engineering — translates detection rules across SIEM/EDR query languages and drafts rules from threat reports.

agents.name: VirusTotal Code Insight
agents.description: Google's AI feature that explains what submitted code and scripts actually do, summarizing malicious behavior in natural language.

agents.name: Google Sec-Gemini
agents.description: Google's experimental security-specialist model combining Gemini reasoning with near-real-time threat intelligence.

agents.name: garak
agents.description: NVIDIA's LLM vulnerability scanner — probes models for injection, jailbreaks, data leakage, and toxicity. Think nmap for LLMs.

agents.name: PyRIT
agents.description: Microsoft's Python Risk Identification Toolkit for automated generative-AI red teaming, built by the Microsoft AI Red Team.

agents.name: promptfoo
agents.description: LLM red-teaming and eval framework — adversarial testing, jailbreak and injection probes, and CI gates for AI applications.

agents.name: LLM Guard
agents.description: Security toolkit that sanitizes and validates LLM inputs and outputs — prompt-injection detection, PII redaction, content policies.

agents.name: Rebuff
agents.description: Self-hardening prompt-injection detector using heuristics, a dedicated LLM check, canary tokens, and a vector store of known attacks.

agents.name: NeMo Guardrails
agents.description: NVIDIA toolkit for adding programmable safety and security rails to LLM applications and conversational agents.

agents.name: PurpleLlama
agents.description: Meta's umbrella of LLM security tools — Llama Guard moderation, CodeShield insecure-code filtering, and CyberSecEval benchmarks.

agents.name: Giskard
agents.description: Open-source evaluation and security testing that automatically detects performance, bias, and security issues in AI models and agents.

agents.name: DeepTeam
agents.description: LLM red-teaming framework that simulates 40+ attack types against agents and chatbots, mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10 and NIST AI RMF.

agents.name: Agentic Radar
agents.description: Scanner for agentic workflows (LangGraph, CrewAI, n8n, OpenAI Agents) that maps dependencies, detects vulnerabilities, and audits tool use.

agents.name: agentgateway
agents.description: Rust data plane for agentic AI — authentication, authorization, guardrails, and observability for MCP tool calls and agent-to-agent traffic.

agents.name: NVIDIA NemoClaw
agents.description: Reference stack that runs always-on agents like OpenClaw inside NVIDIA OpenShell sandboxes — isolation, declarative policy, and routed or fully local inference.

agents.name: Vanta AI Agent
agents.description: AI agent for continuous compliance — automates evidence collection, policy gap analysis, and SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audit preparation.

agents.name: Drata AI
agents.description: Compliance automation with AI that maps controls, drafts policies, and answers security questionnaires.

agents.name: CAI (Cybersecurity AI)
agents.description: Open framework for building bug-bounty-ready cybersecurity agents, with hundreds of built-in tools and real-world CTF pedigree.

agents.name: CrewAI
agents.description: Role-based multi-agent framework — a common foundation for security crews (triage analyst + threat hunter + reporter).

agents.name: LangGraph
agents.description: Stateful agent-orchestration graphs, widely used for security workflows that need checkpoints, retries, and human-in-the-loop gates.

agents.name: Microsoft AutoGen
agents.description: Multi-agent conversation framework from Microsoft Research — the basis for many autonomous SOC and code-analysis prototypes.

agents.name: MCP Reference Servers
agents.description: The open standard for wiring agents to tools — reference servers connect models to filesystems, GitHub, databases, and more.

agents.name: MCP for Security
agents.description: Collection of MCP servers for security tooling — nmap, ffuf, masscan, sqlmap — so any MCP-capable agent can drive them.

agents.name: Semgrep MCP
agents.description: Official MCP server exposing Semgrep scanning to AI agents and coding assistants.

agents.name: Fabric
agents.description: Open framework of crowdsourced AI patterns, including security staples like analyze_threat_report, create_stride_threat_model, and write_semgrep_rule.

agents.name: OpenClaw
agents.description: Self-hosted personal AI assistant and agent runtime with a huge skills ecosystem — commonly hardened with sandboxes like NemoClaw for safe operation.
